notes: Rejected 16 candidates, mostly for being too elaborate for 1853-70 (the '1870s-90s curve' the brief warns about): 11 rue Boissiere (full lion atlantes + mascaron under a balcony, Beaux-Arts scale), 84 rue du Temple (isolated arched mascaron keystones on plain ashlar -- reads as an older 17th-18th c. Marais hotel treatment, not Second Empire), 50-52 rue Notre-Dame-de-Lorette 'facade' shot (round-arched windows with full Corinthian orders and near-continuous mascaron roundels on two registers -- too rich and too continuous to be the period default), Boulevard Magenta nos. 5/50/52/56 (four separate images, all with nude caryatid/atlante figures, cartouches, lion heads -- unambiguously the ornate 1880s-1900s register, not a plain 1855-65 percee facade despite the street itself being Second Empire), Immeuble haussmannien 105-107 rue de Rennes (full standing caryatids carrying the balcony -- Belle Epoque scale), 16 rue Etienne-Marcel (percee only cut in the 1880s; dense mascaron-over-every-window facade confirms a later build), Frise rue Friant (polychrome ceramic Art Nouveau tile insert), P1250390 avenue Daumesnil no.30 porte (explicit Art Nouveau organic relief + whiplash iron gate), 76 avenue d'Italie (grotesque grimacing mascaron masks, heavier and more caricatural than the period's restrained heads), Rue de Chateaudun 59 'Royal Trinite' (corner dome/rotonde and curved bowed balconies wrapping the corner -- both explicit post-1882/1884 tells), Place de l'Opera no.2 (domed rounded corner turret, same tell, dropped despite the quarter itself dating to the 1860s), 101 rue de Richelieu (single door-surround shot, console/mask carving reads Louis XIV-XV in weight and rue de Richelieu is largely pre-Haussmann -- too uncertain to keep). A few more (Detail de la facade 76 avenue d'Italie duplicate check, assorted rue Poussin/rue Raffet/rue du General-Delestraint 16e balcony shots surfaced by the 'Balconies in Paris' category) were skipped without full review because street context (16e villa quarter, Auteuil) points firmly to 1900s-1930s eclectic/Art Deco rather than Second Empire. Commons text search on French terms ('agrafe fenetre console immeuble parisien', 'agrafe clef fenetre immeuble Paris') returned zero or only book/PDF scans (La Construction moderne, dictionaries) -- no usable photos came from full-text search; everything usable came from category walks (Category:Windows in Paris, Category:Haussmannian architecture in Paris, Category:Balconies in Paris) plus direct title lookups. Dating: Commons gives photograph capture dates only, never construction dates, so 'year' is left blank for every image; klass is my visual estimate from facade richness, not a sourced fact. The rue Notre-Dame-de-Lorette window (06) is kept because the single-window crop is unimpeachable as an example of pediment+console+balcon-filant+diminished-floor-above, but the building's construction date could not be confirmed and may sit close to either edge of the 1853-70 bracket -- flagged klass 'unknown' for that reason. Coverage gap: no image in the kept set clearly shows ground-floor bossage/rustication in isolation (sommerard31 shows it in the wider facade shot only); no clean isolated agrafe/keystone-only macro was found that wasn't attached to an over-elaborate mascaron assembly.

images.title: 34 rue Jean-Baptiste-Pigalle, window detail 05
images.author: Coyau
images.shows: Moulded architrave and plain cornice over a window with simple balcon filant ironwork below -- the canonical restrained Second Empire surround with no mascaron.

images.title: 34 rue Jean-Baptiste-Pigalle, window detail 06
images.author: Coyau
images.shows: An upper-floor window with a small triangular fronton and a modest acanthus-and-rosette relief in the tympanum, plain shutters, no balcony -- direct evidence of ornament diminishing on higher floors versus the piano-nobile treatment.

images.title: Balcon d'un immeuble parisien
images.author: besopha (Flickr)
images.shows: Full window opening: triangular pediment with a shell cartouche in the tympanum on console brackets, dentilled cornice, moulded architrave, and a dense cast-iron balcon filant with heart/quatrefoil scrollwork below -- a textbook console-and-fronton-over-balcon assembly.

images.title: 31 rue Du Sommerard
images.author: LPLT
images.shows: Whole corner facade showing the diminution rule end to end: pedimented 2nd-floor windows over a balustraded balcon filant, plainer moulded surrounds at 3rd floor, simple surrounds above, bossage/rustication at the arcaded ground floor shopfront, and a straight 45-degree comble with pedimented dormers on top.

images.title: 53 rue Blanche
images.author: Pline
images.shows: Full flat-plane facade across five floors: small plain rosette medallions (not full mascaron faces) at the spandrels of the two main floors, continuous cast-iron balconies at multiple levels, and visibly plainer top-floor windows -- ornament kept sparing and diminishing rather than dense.

images.title: 50-52 rue Notre-Dame-de-Lorette, window detail
images.author: Coyau
images.shows: Complete window opening in one frame: triangular pediment on console brackets, egg-and-dart and dentil moulding, full architrave with sill/appui, cast-iron balcon filant below the sash, and a plainer shuttered window above it showing the upper-floor diminution. Kept for how completely it frames the opening even though the building's exact construction date could not be confirmed (klass left unknown).

images.title: Paris windows and dormer windows, haussmannian facade
images.author: Vania teofilo
images.shows: Straight 45-degree comble with plain rectangular dormers above a balcon filant, and below it Corinthian-capital console brackets crowning plain window surrounds -- the roofline-to-window relationship the diminution rule depends on.

images.title: Rue Halevy, 12
images.author: Tangopaso
images.shows: Whole corner block facade near the Opera quarter: straight mansard roofline, arcaded rusticated ground floor with voussoired arches, continuous balcon filant at two levels, pilastered piano nobile, and consistent floor-to-floor treatment continuing across the party wall to the left -- good context shot for how the window-surround programme sits inside the whole elevation.

images.title: Rue Halevy 069
images.author: Vania teofilo
images.shows: Close view straight up the facade: two dormers with plain straight triangular pediments (not curved -- the pre-1884 comble type) sitting above a dense cast-iron balcon filant with rosette/heart motifs and a modillion cornice.

images.title: 19 rue Auber
images.author: Guilhem Vellut
images.shows: Two windows with matching triangular frontons on console brackets and a palmette-frieze architrave over a shared balcon filant, plus a single restrained male-mask keystone over the arched ground-floor entry below -- shows mascarons used sparingly (one, at the door) rather than on every opening.

images.title: 164 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honore
images.author: Thomon
images.shows: Multi-floor facade with cartouche-topped pediments and a full balustrade balcon filant at the 2nd floor, a simpler cartouche treatment at the 3rd, and plain surrounds with small console brackets at the 4th -- a clean four-floor progression of diminishing ornament over a scrolled-console entry arch.
